about:
World Wide Auto Parts of Madison, Inc., doing business as World Wide Import Auto Parts, operates from a 15,000-square-foot facility in Madison, Wisconsin. The company focuses on supplying parts for imported cars and trucks, with a particular emphasis on new old stock (NOS) components sourced from original equipment manufacturers.

The business maintains an extensive inventory of NOS parts from brands such as Lucas, Girling, Bosch, and Nippon Denso, as well as from defunct suppliers like Repco and Vera. In addition to distribution, the company remanufactures lever shock absorbers in-house for British and European vehicles, redesigning them to eliminate leaks and backing them with a guarantee. It also stocks current-model parts through direct relationships with suppliers including Beck/Arnley, Centric Parts, and ITM Engine Components.

Customers range from classic-car restorers to owners of late-model imports. The catalog covers British marques such as Triumph, MG, and Morris; French lines including Citroën and Peugeot; German brands like Mercedes-Benz and Volkswagen; Italian makes such as Alfa Romeo and Ferrari; Japanese models from Datsun, Toyota, and Honda; Korean, Swedish, and Yugoslavian vehicles; and even discontinued lines like the Yugo. The company also serves repair shops seeking hard-to-find hydraulic and electrical components from original manufacturers like Girling and Lockheed.

The company differentiates itself through its deep NOS inventory, in-house remanufacturing capability for lever shocks, and direct access to OE supply chains for both obsolete and current production parts.
